set.body:
Scheduling lane: closed. Governing plan: docs/refactor/PLAN.md.

Current disposition, 2026-09-19: Acceptance consolidated into canonical clock integration bd-01M2WTGF981AY7RCN8QC42JSPT. This closure removes duplicate scheduling, not implementation work.

Historical finding and scope retained below; current acceptance ownership above governs.

Extend TimebaseRepair.Record (TimebaseRepair.scala:53) to carry what MediaManifest needs, and build MediaManifest's MEASUREMENTS from it.

1. Parse presentationEditionIdentity.parts[*]: partId, presentationOrdinal, sha256, video.durationTicks, video.ticksPerSecond. MediaManifest's durations, tick rate, run boundary (run1EndRow), row count and part ids come from the record, not from literals.
2. Fold in review silent fields 8-10: the crosswalk's certifies / doesNotCertify, whyNotRepaired and explicitlyNotUsed. The file header (TimebaseRepair.scala:6-21) says the record carries them; Record parsed none, so the record's central scientific restriction could be inverted with every test green (measured). At minimum parse and assert them: a record declaring certifies=media-reachability, or naming the repaired notebook clock as usable for media, must REFUSE. Whether they also travel on the Atlas is the implementer's call.
3. The HASHES are NOT decided here (decision sibling). Until it lands, leave them as they are: test-bound literals.

Tests: every new field is load-bearing, proved by mutating the committed JSON BY JSON PATH with each mutation asserted to have applied. (First-textual-occurrence replacement hit the wrong section once in this line of work and produced a false result.) The existing internal-consistency test, "the repair record agrees with itself about every part extent", stays.
set.title: C1: extend TimebaseRepair.Record with the edition parts and the scientific restrictions; build MediaManifest's measurements from it
